notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR11: lines a REPLACE introduces take 'the indicator area of the introduced lines contains the same character as the line on which the text being replaced begins', a long literal gets continuation lines, and 'If replacement requires the continued literal to be continued on a debugging line, the program is in error.' CopyProcessor.ApplyReplacements replaces text-words in the logical text (each replacement takes the origin of the line its match began on) and DebuggingLineRewriter.DebugLines hides or keeps only the tokens on the D carrier's own line, so neither half of the debugging-line arm holds. Probes (work-rr-04): witness shape, an 80/100-character continued pseudo-text-2 literal replacing a word on an ordinary line, displays whole (p11c, correct, as is p11e's short literal on a D line); b) the error arm: the same 100-character literal replacing XLIT on a D line under WITH DEBUGGING MODE compiles and prints it (p11b, no diagnostic); d) a multi-line pseudo-text-2 replacing a word on a D line WITHOUT the mode: p11g prints THREE..SEVEN and END (expected END only), p11h 'ADD 1 TO WS-N / ADD 2 TO WS-N' prints 3 (expected 1): only the first introduced line is hidden. With the mode (p11d) all seven print, which is right. The sibling §1985:XII.2.4 GR11 (COPY REPLACING into a D-line copybook) fails the same two ways (p11f accepts, p11i prints 3). Classes a, e, f do not reach text manipulation; c: the 2002+ text no longer has the rule. kb/Work PB5382 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-reread2/rr-04.json).

next.reason: 1985: "the indicator area of the introduced lines contains the same character as the line on which the text being replaced begins"; 2023: "shall be in logical free-form reference format. Text-words inserted ... are placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format". Same subject, placing inserted text, but 2023 uses logical free-form: no indicator area, no added continuation lines, no error for a literal continued onto a debugging line.
